samples.text: Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, we must also prepare for the next great transformation, that of artificial intelligence, AI, which could become one of the greatest accelerators of human development. AI can broaden access to knowledge, improve health systems, support agricultural workers, and make state administrations more efficient. Having said that, AI can also amplify or exacerbate existing divides. If Africa was to solely consume technologies designed and controlled outside the continent, a new form of dependence could emerge linked to data infrastructure, computing power, and critical technologies. We must avoid this scenario. Therefore, Benin is in favor of international AI governance that's inclusive, responsible, and development-oriented. Africa should not just be a market for frontier technologies. It should also be a platform for design, innovation, and production. This is the prerequisite for AI to become not a new driver of divisions, but a tool for achieving emancipation, progress, and shared development. Excellencies, ladies and gentlemen, trust in international institutions is also linked to the trust people bestow upon their own institutions. For its part, Benin is continuing the process of consolidating our institutions and our democratic framework with full respect for our constitution and our legal order. We deem stability, public responsibility and citizen participation, we deem them essential preconditions for sustainable development. Our experience confirms our conviction: robust institutions, are one of the pillars of peace infrastructure. We stand convinced that while we might have different national trajectories, these trajectories should nevertheless converge towards the same end goal, giving all people the necessary conditions for them to be able to forge their future, living in peace, dignity, and stability. Mr. President, if I may, I would now like to address a dimension that lies at the very heart of Benin's identity. Benin is a land of memory, forged from greatness and resistance. But we also have a very tragic, painful history, that of daughters and sons torn away from their land, separated from their families, and sent to different parts of the world, scattered. This history has left very deep wounds. It also, through generations, created a diaspora.
